title: Generative Conformal Prediction with Optimized Coverage Allocation
claim: Prior methods use a single rigid region that over-covers multimodal data; ours allocates rank-based radii for tighter, flexible sets.
layout: 5 panels in a row, left-to-right, shared legend at right, red rank annotations
description: A single row of five square panels, each showing the same blue-gradient density with three modes: a dark one at lower left, a lighter one at upper left, and a lighter one at right. A green dot marks the true response in the dark mode. Panel titles are CP, CP (Bonferroni), Covariance Weighted CP, PCP and ORCA. CP uses one huge dashed circle covering everything. Bonferroni uses a large dashed rectangle. Covariance Weighted CP uses a dashed ellipse. PCP uses three equal-size dashed circles around black sample dots. In ORCA the circles have different radii, with red dashed lines from the green dot to each black sample and labels r=1, r=2 and r=3. The circle is largest in the dense mode and smaller in the sparse ones. A legend at far right shows the density p, the region C_k, the true response Y_i and the generated samples Ŷ_{i,k}. The eye goes first to the big loose regions on the left, then to the tighter ORCA panel with red annotations.
caption: Comparison of conformal prediction methods and their prediction regions. From left to right: standard CP [ref], Bonferroni-corrected CP [ref], Covariance Weighted CP [ref], PCP [ref], and ORCA (our method). The background gradient shows the multimodal data distribution. ORCA adjusts circle radii via ranking—larger in dense areas, smaller in sparse ones—yielding more efficient and flexible prediction sets. Green dots denote true responses ($Y_i$), black dots are generated samples ($\hat{Y}_{i,k}$), and dashed lines mark prediction boundaries ($\mathcal{C}_k$).
abstract: Conformal prediction provides model-agnostic uncertainty quantification with guaranteed coverage, but conventional methods often yield overly conservative uncertainty sets, particularly in multimodal or heterogeneous settings. This inefficiency arises from two sources: (i) limited expressiveness of the predictive model and (ii) simplistic nonconformity score design. Most existing approaches advance only one of these axes, leaving the other underexplored. We propose generative conformal prediction with Optimized Ranking and Coverage Allocation (ORCA), a three-stage framework that advances both aspects jointly. ORCA leverages generative models to capture the full conditional distribution and introduces a rank-dependent optimization procedure that adaptively allocates coverage for efficiency while maintaining validity. We cast this coverage allocation as an optimization problem, derive an exact mixed-integer linear programming formulation, and show that the solution converges asymptotically to the oracle density-level set. Across synthetic, semi-synthetic, and real datasets, ORCA produces substantially more efficient uncertainty sets than state-of-the-art baselines, demonstrating robust gains in scenarios where conventional conformal prediction methods fail.
